questions.stem: What role does a data hub play in enterprise data architecture?
options: A new type of storage system replacing the data lake
A new analytical framework for machine learning
The central integration and distribution point connecting analytical platforms with operational systems
A department-level data mart
A tool for scraping external websites
questions.explanation: A data hub is not another storage system or analytical framework; it is the central integration and distribution point that connects analytical platforms with operational systems.

questions.stem: Which category of enterprise system includes ERP, CRM and core banking applications?
options: Data warehouses
Data lakes
Operational systems (OLTP)
Semantic layers
Data hubs
questions.explanation: Operational systems (OLTP) are the core enterprise applications such as ERP, CRM and core banking systems.

questions.stem: What practical problem does the division of enterprise systems into OLTP, data warehouse and data lake create?
options: Data cannot be encrypted across systems
Insights such as KPIs, predictions and classifications are hard to share back with the applications that drive day-to-day business
Warehouses cannot store history
OLTP systems become too slow
Data lakes cannot store unstructured data
questions.explanation: The division makes it hard to share BI and analytics results, KPIs, predictions, classifications and insights, back with the very applications that run the business.

questions.stem: In the core banking example, which of the following is NOT one of the three separate pipelines connecting to the core banking system?
options: Integration with the mobile or online banking application
Integration with the data warehouse for reporting and data mining
Integration with the data lake for advanced analytics and data science
Integration with a social media scraping tool
Integration with the data lake for machine learning models
questions.explanation: The three pipelines are to the mobile or online banking application, the data warehouse and the data lake; social media scraping is not one of them.

questions.stem: How does a data hub change the way applications connect to data sources?
options: Every application builds its own pipeline to every source
Applications connect once to the hub, which in turn connects to all underlying datastores
Applications connect directly to the data lake only
Applications export data to spreadsheets
Applications must be rewritten in a common language
questions.explanation: Instead of every application building its own pipeline to every source, applications connect once to the hub, and the hub connects to OLTP, data warehouse and data lake.

questions.stem: In what forms can a data hub publish insights from BI, machine learning and data mining for enterprise applications?
options: Printed reports
APIs, data services or event streams
Tape backups
Star schemas
Encrypted archives
questions.explanation: The hub design allows insights to be published as APIs, data services or event streams consumable by enterprise applications.

questions.stem: How does a data hub go beyond the serving or semantic layer of a data warehouse or lakehouse?
options: It stores more history
It exposes curated data only to BI tools
It operationalises the same data, making it available to applications such as mobile banking, customer service platforms or ERP systems
It replaces dimensional modelling
It removes the need for a data lake
questions.explanation: Serving layers expose curated data for BI tools; the hub operationalises the same data for applications such as mobile banking, customer service platforms, ERP or social media integration.

questions.stem: What governance benefit comes from centralising access through a data hub?
options: Data products are distributed consistently with proper lineage, access controls and usage policies
Governance can be skipped because the hub is trusted
Every application manages its own security
History is preserved automatically
Data is stored in a single country
questions.explanation: By centralising access, the hub ensures data products are distributed consistently with proper lineage, access controls and usage policies, preventing ad hoc pipelines.

questions.stem: What problems arise from the proliferation of ad hoc pipelines that a data hub is meant to prevent?
options: Faster delivery and lower cost
Duplication, inconsistencies and security risks
Loss of unstructured data
Excessive normalisation
Slower OLTP transactions
questions.explanation: Ad hoc pipelines often result in duplication, inconsistencies and security risks, which the hub's centralised, governed integration prevents.

questions.stem: What kind of exchange does a data hub create between analytical and transactional worlds?
options: A one-way flow from operational systems into the warehouse
A two-way exchange, letting insights from warehouses and lakes flow back into operational systems
A batch-only overnight transfer
A read-only mirror of the data lake
No exchange; it isolates the two worlds
questions.explanation: The hub enables insights from data warehouses and data lakes to flow back into operational systems, creating a two-way exchange between the analytical and transactional worlds.
